# Caddy — multiple-root-context

Two independent app instances, each running at /, exposed under different prefixes (/ui1 and /ui2). Each handle_path strips its own prefix and rescopes Location and Set-Cookie on the way out, which is what keeps the two csrfToken cookies apart without telling either app where it is published.

Proxy URL on `http://localhost:9090`: `/ui1/,/ui2/`

## Configuration

See [docker-compose.yml](./docker-compose.yml) for service definitions.

Caddy site block (`caddy/http/multiple-root-context/vaadin.caddyfile`), mounted as
`/etc/caddy/vaadin.caddyfile`:

```caddyfile
# Two independent apps, both at their own backend's root, published under
# different prefixes. Neither backend has a context path: the prefix exists only
# in the public URL, and handle_path removes it.
#
# Each app's Location and Set-Cookie are rescoped into its own prefix on the way
# out, the way NGINX does it with proxy_cookie_path. That is what keeps the two
# csrfToken cookies apart: both apps issue it under the same name, and without
# the rewrite each would clobber the other's on /, breaking Hilla for whichever
# app was visited first. Compare traefik/http/multiple-root-context, which
# cannot rewrite a response and has to tell each app its prefix instead.
:80 {
	import common

	redir /ui1 /ui1/ 308
	redir /ui2 /ui2/ 308

	handle_path /ui1/* {
		reverse_proxy vaadin1:8080 {
			header_down Location ^(https?://[^/]+)?/(.*)$ $1/ui1/$2
			header_down Set-Cookie ^(.*;\s*[Pp]ath=)/(;.*)?$ $1/ui1$2
		}
	}

	handle_path /ui2/* {
		reverse_proxy vaadin2:8080 {
			header_down Location ^(https?://[^/]+)?/(.*)$ $1/ui2/$2
			header_down Set-Cookie ^(.*;\s*[Pp]ath=)/(;.*)?$ $1/ui2$2
		}
	}

	handle {
		respond 404
	}
}
```

The global options and the `common` snippet this file imports (the
access log and the compression allowlist) come from the shared
[Caddyfile](../../Caddyfile), mounted read-only over the image's own
`/etc/caddy/Caddyfile`. It imports this file, so the two only load as a pair.
